title: Canto 5: The Creative Impetus - Title, Artist and Source Pictures Canto 5
content:
Title, Artist and Source Pictures Canto 5

5.1

Title: The picture shows Lord Brahmā riding the swan. Murshidabad, 19th. century.

Artist: Unknown

Source: The Hare Kṛṣṇas, harekrsna.com

5.2

Title: The painting is titled: ‘Vasanti’.

Artist: Raja Ravi Varma

Source: Wikipedia.org

5.3

Title: The painting is titled: ‘Devotion to the tulsi plant, sweet basil. A lady ascetic.’ Rajput, 18th. century.

Artist: Unknown

Source: The British Museum - britishmuseum.org

5.4

Title: The painting is titled: ‘The anointment of King Ṛṣabha’. Leaf from a

Jain Kalpasutra. Ca. 1500.

Artist: Unknown

Source: Private collection. Indianminiaturepaintings.co.uk

5.5

Title: The painting is a Jain miniature titled: ‘Layman in worshiping posture’. Palm Leaf. Western India.

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet

5.6

Title: The picture is a statue of Lord Ṛṣabhadeva excavated in Khahujar, the way the Jains like to see him as their first Tirthankara.

Source: Wikipedia.org

5.7

Title: The modern Hindu image shows Lord Hari standing on the lotus of the heart.

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet

5.8

Title: The picture of deer in a forest as the love of Bharata, is a detail of a painting titled: ‘Ragini Todi’.

Artist: Kailash Raj

Source: exoticindiaart.com © Exotic India Art. Used with permission.

5.9

Title: The picture is of a tantric form of the Hindu goddess Kālī. Folio from a Book of Iconography, 17th century, Nepal, Himalayas.

Source: Courtesy Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA). Lacma.org

5.10

Title: The title of the imag is: 226. Long Palanquin (pp. 460-62).

Source: The image is from: “A Portrait of the Hindus: Balthazar Solvyns & the European Image of India 1760-1824”. Solvyns, Les Hindoûs: III.9.4.

© From the collection of prof. R.L. Hardgrave, University of Texas. Used with permission.

5.11

Title: ‘Supersoul’

Artist: Johannes Ptok (Aka Janmanalaya)

Source: Consciousart gallery & Ptok.se

5.12

Title: The picture is a vintage Gītā illustration titled: “Reward of exclusive thought”.

Artist: Unknown.

Source: Internet

5.13

Title: Depressed person.

Artist: William Blake

Source: wikipedia.org & blakearchive.org

5.14

Title first painting: (digital focus) of an illustration of William Blake, to Dante’s Inferno: Hell XII.

Artist: William Blake

Source: wikipedia.org & blakearchive.org

5.15

Title: 'A Vaishnava priest in conversation with two devotees', Bundikalam, late 18th century.

Artist: Unknown

Bron/Courtesy: Vahini org Gallery

5.16

Title: The picture of Brahmā as the center of the galactic whorl with Mount Meru is a digital collage.

Artist: Anand Aadhar

Source: Internet

5.17

Title: ‘The Birth of Gangā’.

Artist: Khitindra Nāth Mazumdar

Source: ‘Myths of the Hindus and Buddhists’, Ballantine Press, Oct. 1913

5.18

Title: ‘Kṛṣṇa and Gopis; Kamadeva, God of Desire’. Folio from a Gita Govinda (Song of the Cowherd), circa 1585. India, Gujarat, South Asia.

Source/Courtesy: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA), collectionsonline.lacma.org

5.19

Title: Collage of a vintage painting of Hanumān praying

Artist: Anand Aadhar

Source: Internet

5.20

Title: The first picture is titled: ‘Jambhu Dvipa Cosmology’. It is a Jainist diagram of the division of the one cosmos, with at the center the heart and the mystical mountain Meru, surrounded by seas and rivers (15th century).

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet

5.21

Title: The Sun God Surya

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet

5.22

Title: The collage of the image on this page is by Anand Aadhar

Source: Internet

5.23

Title: The collage of the image on this page is by Anand Aadhar

Source: Internet

5.24

Title: Painting of the nether world of beauty in which one is bound by illusion

Artist: Seema Kohli (artist and philosopher living in New Delhi, India)

Source: Wikimedia.org

5.25

Title: The picture is a detail of a Hindu picture of Ananta Vishnu

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet

5.26

Title: “Hell (Hölle)” Hortus Deliciarum.

Artist: Herrad von Landsberg (about 1180)

Source: Wikimedia.org
